name: IEC pulse-triggered (master-slave) JK flip-flop
summary: JK bistable whose outputs carry postponed marks: they change when the clock pulse ends, not at its start.
description: A pulse-triggered or master-slave JK flip-flop is drawn with a static C1 input and postponed output marks at Q and its complement. The data must be set up before the clock pulse starts and held while C1 is active; the outputs change when C1 returns to its initial level.

Older TTL designs and some relay-logic equivalents use this behaviour. When reviewing, the presence of the postponed mark tells you that J and K must not change during the clock pulse, a stricter rule than for edge-triggered devices.
If the C1 input also carries a dynamic mark, the device is the data lock-out type, which samples on the edge but still postpones the output.
readingNotes: Postponed marks at outputs indicate pulse triggering.
A dynamic C1 together with postponed outputs indicates data lock-out.
drawingChecklist: Draw postponed marks next to both outputs.
Show C1 as static unless data lock-out is intended.
distinction: The edge-triggered JK flip-flop has a dynamic C1 and no postponed marks.
